rationale: Provides an open-source silicon Root of Trust (RoT) with secure boot, cryptographic key management, and hardware identity support.
Enables verifiable hardware root of trust and cryptographic chip lifecycle tracking to secure the chip supply chain against tampering.
Collects always-on hardware performance counters and GPU/CPU telemetry to detect anomalous behavior in training clusters.
Monitors and logs fine-grained CPU and GPU resource utilization per job for cluster usage governance and auditing.
Collects low-overhead per-GPU telemetry (power, temperature, utilization, clocks) across accelerator clusters for anomaly detection.
Provides aggregated scale-out resource consumption and memory metrics across cluster hosts and user jobs for usage auditing.
Implements hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) on RISC-V architectures using Physical Memory Protection (PMP).
Leverages chip-level RISC-V PMP and OpenSBI security mechanisms to provide secure enclave execution and memory isolation.
Implements Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) key extraction and bit selection mechanisms using off-the-shelf SRAM for hardware identity.
Implements SRAM PUF fingerprint extraction on microcontroller hardware to generate authentication tokens without stored credentials.
Provides vendor-agnostic APIs to collect and verify attestation reports, quotes, and integrity measurements from TEEs.
Accesses chip-level security measurements, secure boot event records, and hardware quotes across TPMs and confidential computing hardware.
Provides a C++ evaluation framework to analyze hardware implementations against side-channel leakage and fault injection attacks.
Provides a dynamic instrumentation and statistical framework to detect, localize, and quantify microarchitectural side-channel leaks.
Emulates binary execution and generates side-channel traces to evaluate code resistance against side-channel analysis and fault injection.
Implements constant-time execution wrappers and utilities in Rust to prevent timing side-channel attacks.
Implements integrity-protected workload execution inside hardware TEEs (AMD SEV-SNP and Intel TDX) with attestation report generation.
Implements CA certificate issuance cryptographically bound to hardware TPM Endorsement Keys for hardware-anchored authentication.
Builds a verified chain-of-trust based on UEFI Secure Boot and dm-verity cryptographic hash tree verification.
Protects filesystem binaries and edge model data from persistent tampering using dm-verity verified squashfs images.
